record.paper_title: Five open problems in theory of quantum information
record.original_question: In the six-dimensional complex Hilbert space H_6, either construct a set of at least four mutually unbiased bases or prove that a complete set of seven mutually unbiased bases does not exist. A mutually unbiased-basis set consists of orthonormal bases such that vectors from distinct bases have squared inner product 1/6; the general upper bound in dimension 6 is seven bases, but only triples are currently known in the cited literature.

evidence.quote: Problem 2: Construct a set of at least 4 mutually unbiased bases in dimension six or prove that there are no 7 MUBs in H6.
In particular, for N = 6 a complete set would consist of seven MUBs, but up till now only solutions containing three bases were found [51–60].
There exist 4, 5, and 6 MUBs in dimensionsN = 3, 4 and 5, respectively. How many MUBs there exist forN = 6?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_6 = \mathbb{C}^6$ with the standard Hermitian inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$. Two orthonormal bases $\mathcal{B} = \{e_1,\dots,e_6\}$ and $\mathcal{B}' = \{f_1,\dots,f_6\}$ of $\mathcal{H}_6$ are called mutually unbiased if
$$|\langle e_i, f_j\rangle|^2 = \frac{1}{6} \quad \text{for all } i,j \in \{1,\dots,6\}.$$
A family $\{\mathcal{B}_1,\dots,\mathcal{B}_m\}$ of orthonormal bases of $\mathcal{H}_6$ is called a set of $m$ mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) if every pair $\mathcal{B}_a, \mathcal{B}_b$ with $a \neq b$ is mutually unbiased. It is known that any such family satisfies $m \le 7$, and that families of size $m = 3$ exist.

Establish at least one of the following:
(a) construct an explicit set of $m \ge 4$ mutually unbiased bases in $\mathcal{H}_6$; or
(b) prove that there is no set of $7$ mutually unbiased bases in $\mathcal{H}_6$.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of 4 or more mutually unbiased bases in dimension six remains a famous open problem. Strong numerical evidence (Hadamard-matrix searches, polynomial optimization approaches in 2025) suggests no set of 4 MUBs exists, and the conjecture is that the maximum is 3, but no proof is known. Recent 2025 work formulates the question as a commuting polynomial optimization problem and notes that a 2017 lemma by Chen et al., previously used to constrain 4-MUB structure, contains a flaw that invalidates several follow-up theorems.

status_evidence.title: Mutually unbiased bases - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Dimension 6 is the smallest dimension for which the number of mutually unbiased bases is not known.

status_evidence.title: Mutually unbiased bases as a commuting polynomial optimization problem
status_evidence.snippet: Such an algorithm would eventually solve the open question in dimension six with finite memory, although it still remains intractable.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2025 work confirms d=6 MUB question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Reply to Comment on 'Product states and Schmidt rank of MUBs in dimension six'
status_evidence.snippet: A 2017 lemma by Chen et al. on 4-MUB structure in C^6 had a flawed proof, invalidating later theorems.
status_evidence.claim: No proof yet that 4 MUBs do not exist in dimension 6.
